title: Turning feedback into fixes
idea: Iteration turns each review comment into a decision: reproduce it as a failing check, fix the one class responsible, re-run everything, and record what you decided.
points: Triage each comment by id: fix, defer, or decline; blocking ones usually become fixes.
Write the failing check first, so the comment becomes a test that cannot regress.
Fix in the class that owns the rule: `BookingService.cancel` owns cancel rules.
Re-run the full suite after each fix, not only the new check.

hero.title: One review comment, start to close

edges.caption: Give the comment an id and decide its fate before touching code.
Accepted: reproduce the gap as a check that fails today.
Change only the class that owns the rule, here the service's `cancel` with a clock.
Run every check, so the fix cannot break booking or search.
Record the decision so the next reviewer sees why it changed.
A red check sends you back to the fix, not to the comment.

code.title: Feedback as a check
code.caption: Review comment FB-4 becomes two named checks: an ended booking is refused and an upcoming one still cancels.

walk.text: An injected clock fixes now at 11:00, so one booking has ended and one is upcoming.
The check carries the feedback id, so its output links back to the review comment.
A second check guards the other side: the fix must not block future bookings.
The runner compares stable error codes, not messages, so wording changes do not break it.
Owner checks came from c11-t04. The new `if` compares the end with the clock.

pitfalls: Fixing silently without a check; the same bug returns in the next refactor.
Accepting every comment; a declined comment with a written reason is a valid outcome.

quiz.q: Delete lines 89-91 (the end-time `if`). What does the first check print?
options: FAIL FB-4 ended booking cannot cancel -> OK
PASS FB-4 ended booking cannot cancel -> INVALID_SLOT
FAIL FB-4 ended booking cannot cancel -> NOT_OWNER
quiz.why: Without the guard, `cancel` removes the ended booking and returns, so the runner records OK. OK is not the expected INVALID_SLOT, so the check fails.

takeaway: Each comment becomes a check, a focused fix and a recorded decision.

starters: How do I decide whether to fix, defer or decline a review comment?
What should a decision log entry for my booking system look like?
How do I handle two reviewers who give opposite feedback?
